profile.headline: Embedded SW Engineer
profile.summary:
I wrote that intro below a long time ago. In 2010 or so a marketing bloke said not to change it. I didn't. 
I still love the embedded space. While some shift of focus has occurred, I look back and it all still mostly applies. 
It is still engineering.  

--

Software/Hardware marriage counselor.  
I am an expert in the area of getting software to fall in love with the hardware that it needs to get along with. 

System requirements, architecture, design and implementation of many obtuse, run of the mill or grand ideas. This includes everything in the system software from power on to the kernel and all drivers running in concerted symphony.

The child in me loves the hard problems, the big ideas, the chance to work on things that help society (medical, energy related, research for a better the world), seeing the first LED come on, the beauty of  the very first "Hello World" barked out of the new system. 
The adult in me insists on stability, security and reliability of that system.

Specialties and philosophies: 
- Embedded Systems, anything near the hardware
- Linux kernel, middleware and drivers. (I prefer working in the RTOS/bare metal world, so linux has atrophied)
- Bootloaders, board bringup, new chip bring up.
- Agile processes. I did not drink the entire bottle of agile kool-aid, but I took a decent sized slurp.
- ARMv4 onwards to Armv8 + Trustzone, including Cortex-M, Cortex-A, Cortex-R
- I believe in testing first, testing during, testing afterwards. The only way to prove requirements are met is to test and verify them. Find problems early. Discover design blunders and poor API definitions before they are tough to fix.
- Process is a good thing, checklists save lives. 
- No matter what the customer thinks, never start thinking about specification/design without requirements for their use cases. Just don't. If you have to, write your own then ask if they will work - get sign off on them. They can change, but change has a cost. Communicate that impacts throughout the process.
- RTOSes and bare metal. I have learned the hard way that feature creep can render bare metal 'super loop' unmanageable, consider an RTOS from the beginning on any project that has more than one provider of requirements. Or any project driven by marketing. On other projects consider using an RTOS anyway. You get a pass on an 8-bit micro. 
- Many battery powered products seem to have BLE lately, so I have been working with that too.  
- Security matters. Integrity matters.

positions.title: Embedded Software Developer
positions.description:
After a few years working on robots, I though it was time to try something else - Project Kuiper.

Project Kuiper is a long-term initiative to launch a constellation of Low Earth Orbit satellites that will provide low-latency, high-speed broadband connectivity to unserved and underserved communities around the world.
